title: APH revocation status list credential (spec 6.3.3.3)
description: The document a notary serves at its DERIVED status endpoint (spec 6.3.3.2), or at a same-origin path a statusListCredential names. A W3C BitstringStatusListCredential profiled by APH for revocation only. Deliberately NOT closed with additionalProperties:false - this is a general W3C artifact that legitimately carries members APH does not read (name, description, ttl, validUntil, renderMethod), and a verifier that refused those would refuse ordinary conformant documents.

@context.description: No APH context term is added by this mechanism: BitstringStatusListEntry and its members are defined by the W3C VC 2.0 context every APH envelope already lists first (spec 6.3.3.1).

id.description: Identifier of this status list credential, when it carries one.

issuer.description: MUST be the same notary DID the endpoint was DERIVED from (spec 6.3.3.2 step 1). Same-origin alone does not make a document authoritative - one host serves many documents, and the path is the envelope's to name - so the list must ALSO be signed by the notary whose mandate is in question. Both W3C spellings are legal: a bare DID string, or an object carrying `id`.

validFrom.description: RFC 3339 issuance instant. A verifier MUST NOT accept a credential whose validFrom is more than 5 minutes before now, allowing the same 60-second clock skew as 8.3 step 6 (spec 6.3.3.3). A notary publishing status MUST re-issue at an interval no greater than 2 minutes, so a conformant verifier always finds a credential inside the bound. A document with no validFrom cannot be checked against the bound and is therefore 6.3.3.4 case 2.

type.description: Checked when present. APH 6.3.3.3 names the purpose, the issuer, the proof and the freshness bound as its normative checks and leaves this member to the W3C profile, so requiring its presence would refuse documents that are conformant as far as APH ever said.

statusPurpose.description: An unrecognized purpose HERE is spec 6.3.3.4 case 2 (APH_E008, the status could not be established), NOT the parse failure the ENVELOPE entry raises for the same word. The asymmetry is deliberate: the envelope entry is APH wire covered by a signature, this document is a fetched foreign artifact.

encodedList.description: Multibase (leading 'u' = base64url, no padding) of the GZIP-compressed bitstring. Bit order is the W3C profile's: index 0 is the MOST SIGNIFICANT bit of the first byte. A bit of 1 means revoked; 0 means not revoked and verification continues. A list too short to contain statusListIndex is 6.3.3.4 case 2 - reading a missing bit as 0 would turn a truncated list into a blanket 'nothing is revoked'.

proof.description: The notary's proof, secured under 8.1/8.2, whose verification method resolves through 8.4 exactly as an envelope proof does (spec 6.3.3.3). This is load-bearing rather than decorative: same-origin permits a different PATH, so a host with any writable path would otherwise let an attacker publish a forged list that satisfies same-origin and simply writes the notary's DID into its own issuer.
